mapName: A Learnable Oceania - Identify Every Country

metas.name: American Samoa - Unique Car
metas.note: • A slightly rusted black truck bed can be seen on the main island of Tutuila.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Australia - Black Give-Way Sign
metas.note:
• Give-way signs in Australia have a white border and black text.

--- NOTE:

  • New Zealand’s give-way signs use red, instead of black, text.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Australia - Bollards
metas.note:
• Australian bollards are white, with a red reflector on the front, and a grey reflector on the back.

--- NOTE:

  • New Zealand uses a bollard where the red reflector wraps around the back, meaning the reflector goes from end to end while the Australian one stops in the middle.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Australia - Eucalyptus Trees
metas.note:
• Eucalyptus trees are by far the most common type of tree in Australia.
  • Their bark is typically light-coloured, with puffy puffy clusters of leaves.

--- NOTE:

  • Their look may vary significantly, depending on your location within the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Australia - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Australia uses almost exclusively white road lines.

--- NOTE:

  • New Zealand can have all white road lines as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Christmas Island - Unique Car
metas.note:
The car coverage was done with a unique Google car:

  • A silver pickup truck, with the bed of the truck visible.
  • Usually, this is all you need to identify Christmas Island.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/christmas-island.

metas.name: Cocos (Keeling) Islands - Unique Car
metas.note: • This unique car with a snorkel at the front right and the edges of the bed visible is found on West Island.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Guam - Car
metas.note:
• The entire Google car is blurred, however an antenna at the front right and a tiny part of the roof rack can be seen.

--- NOTE:

  • You will not see a roof rack on the Northern Mariana Islands Google car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/guam.

metas.name: Guam - Poles
metas.note:
• Poles on Guam are almost always concrete and commonly very thick.

--- NOTE:

  • Northern Mariana Islands typically have wooden poles.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/guam.

metas.name: Guam - Road Reflectors
metas.note: • Both Guam and Northern Mariana Islands often have a very large number of road reflectors.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/guam.

metas.name: New Zealand - Bollards
metas.note:
• Bollards in New Zealand have a red strip which wraps around the top of the bollard.
  • This strip wraps the whole way around the back and part of the front.

--- NOTE:

  • These bollards are unique to New Zealand.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: New Zealand - Poles
metas.note:
• The most common pole type found in New Zealand is made of concrete and has one long indent which runs most of the way up the pole.
  • Most concrete poles have small silver possum guards.
  • You can also see concrete holey poles in New Zealand.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: New Zealand - Red Give-Way Sign
metas.note:
• Give-way signs in New Zealand have a white border and red text.

--- NOTE:

  • Australia’s give-way signs use black text.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: New Zealand - Street Signs
metas.note:
• New Zealand often uses blue street signs with white text, particularly in rural areas.
  • While street signs of other colours can be often seen, blue is by far the most common.

--- NOTE:

  • Australia almost never has blue street signs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Northern Mariana Islands - Close Antenna
metas.note:
• The entire Google car is blurred, however an antenna at the front right can be seen.
  • The antenna is also noticeably closer to the camera than in the Guam Google car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/northern-mariana-islands.

metas.name: Northern Mariana Islands - Poles
metas.note:
• Northern Mariana Islands have wooden poles, frequently with a crossbar at the top.

--- NOTE:

  • Guam typically has concrete poles.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/northern-mariana-islands.

metas.name: Northern Mariana Islands - Road Reflectors
metas.note: • Both Northern Mariana Islands and Guam often have a very large number of road reflectors.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/northern-mariana-islands.
